summary: The word "كَهْرَبٌ" (kahrab) refers to yellow amber. Its origin is Persian, meaning "straw-attracting," due to its electrostatic properties. This term is the root of the modern word "electricity."
lane: كَهْرَبٌ ذ and كَهْرَبَا [or كَهْرُبَا ] A well-known yellow substance; [ yellow amber ]: from the Persian كَاهُ رُبَا , i. e., “ carrying off straw, ” [on account of its electric attraction]. (TA.) See De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., sec. ed., iii. 468: and see حَوَرٌ .
